q: 1. Handles of chains are made up of
explain: The handles of a surveying chain are usually made of brass (a non-magnetic, corrosion resistant material), while the links themselves are of steel or galvanized iron.

q: 2. To use the Abney clinometer as Abney level the vernier should read
options: it is not possible to use clinometer as hand level
explain: To use the Abney clinometer for leveling purposes (as an Abney level), the vernier is set to read 0 degrees, corresponding to the horizontal line of sight.

q: 3. The length of an Engineer's chain is
explain: An Engineer's chain is 100 feet long, divided into 100 links of 1 foot each, distinguishing it from Gunter's chain (66 feet).

q: 4. Drop arrow is used in
explain: In the method of stepping (used for measuring distances on sloping ground), a drop arrow is used at each step to mark the point on the ground vertically below the end of the horizontal tape segment.

q: 5. Ceylon Ghat tracer can read slopes up to
explain: The Ceylon ghat tracer, designed for locating contour gradients on steep hill roads, can read slope ratios ranging from about 1 in 120 to 1 in 6.

q: 6. Pick up the most accurate statement from the following.
options: survey lines in an area should be as many as possible
number of base lines in an area is limited to one
main chain lines should form well conditioned triangles
oblique offsets are inferior to perpendicular offsets
explain: A fundamental principle of chain surveying is that the main survey (chain) lines should be laid out so as to form well-conditioned triangles, ensuring accurate plotting.

q: 7. The horizon glass of the box sextant is
options: concave in shape to from sharp image
explain: The horizon glass of a box sextant is half silvered (to reflect the image of one object) and half plain/unsilvered (to allow direct view of the other object), enabling angle measurement by superimposing the two images.

q: 8. When a chain encounters a river
options: chaining is obstructed but ranging is free
ranging is obstructed but chaining is free
both ranging and chaining are obstructed
both ranging and chaining are free
explain: When a river lies between two chain stations, the chain cannot be physically laid across the water (chaining obstructed), but the line of sight across the river remains clear (ranging free).

q: 9. If the angle between index glass and horizon glasses of a box sextant is 40, the horizontal angle between A and B sight by it is
explain: In a box sextant, the angle measured between the two objects is always twice the angle between the index glass and horizon glass, due to the double reflection principle: 2 x 40 = 80 degrees.

q: 10. Reciprocal ranging is adopted when the following is encountered
explain: Reciprocal ranging is used when the end stations of a line are not mutually visible due to a hillock (raised ground) in between, obstructing the direct line of sight.

q: 11. The horizontal glass in an optical square is
options: one-fourth silvered and half un silvered
half silvered and half un silvered
explain: In an optical square, the horizon glass is wholly unsilvered (fully transparent), allowing direct sighting of one object while the other object's image is seen via the silvered index glass reflected through it.

q: 12. The index glass in an optical square is
options: one-fourth silvered and half un silvered
half silvered and half un silvered
explain: The index glass in an optical square is wholly silvered, so it fully reflects the image of the object sighted through it towards the horizon glass.

q: 13. The instrument, belonging to a class of reflecting instrument is
explain: The box sextant works on the principle of double reflection from two mirrors, making it a reflecting instrument, unlike the line ranger or prismatic compass.

q: 14. In an optical square, the angle between the first incident ray and the last reflected ray is
explain: Due to the 45-degree angle between the two mirrors and the principle of double reflection, the optical square deflects the incident ray through exactly 90 degrees.

q: 15. When the object lies on the left hand side of the chain line, then while taking offset with an optical square, it is held in
explain: For an object on the left of the chain line, the optical square is conventionally held in the right hand, upright, to correctly sight and align the offset.

q: 16. Check lines (or proof lines) in Chain Surveying are essentially required
options: to indicate the accuracy of the survey work
explain: Check lines are measured independently in the field specifically to verify (indicate) the accuracy of the main chain survey framework after plotting.

q: 17. A well conditioned triangle has no angle less than
explain: A well-conditioned triangle in triangulation/chain surveying is one where no angle is less than 30 degrees (and no angle exceeds 120 degrees), minimizing plotting errors.

q: 18. An instrument used to find slopes of ground is
explain: A clinometer is specifically designed to measure the angle of slope (inclination) of the ground.

q: 19. An instrument that can be used as an optical square is
explain: A box sextant, when set to read exactly 90 degrees, can be used in place of an optical square to set out right angles.

q: 20. The construction of optical square is based, on the principle of optical
explain: The optical square works on the principle of double reflection from two mirrors set at 45 degrees to each other, deflecting the line of sight through 90 degrees.

q: 21. The limiting length of an offset does not depend upon
explain: As per the book's answer key, the limiting length of an offset depends on the accuracy required, the method of setting out perpendiculars, and the nature of features surveyed - but not on the scale of plotting.

q: 22. The angle between two plane mirrors of optical square is
explain: The two plane mirrors in an optical square are fixed at exactly 45 degrees to each other to achieve a 90-degree deflection of the line of sight.

q: 23. An angles of 45 with a chain line may be set out with
explain: The french cross-staff has additional slits set at 45 degrees (besides the 90-degree ones), specifically enabling 45-degree offsets to be set out.

q: 24. For taking offsets with an optical square on the right hand side of the chain line, it is held
explain: For an object on the right side of the chain line, the optical square is conventionally held in the right hand, upright, for correct sighting.

q: 25. Correction for pull is
explain: The pull correction to a measured tape length is given by (P-P0)l / AE, where P is the applied pull, P0 the standard pull, l the length, A the cross-sectional area, and E the modulus of elasticity of the tape material.

q: 26. Pick up the most accurate statement from the following
options: survey lines in an area should be as many as possible
number of base lines in an area is limited to one
main chain lines should from well conditioned triangles
oblique offsets are inferior to perpendicular offsets
explain: For accurate chain surveying, the framework of main chain lines should form well-conditioned triangles (angles not less than 30 nor more than 120 degrees), minimizing plotting errors.

q: 27. When a chain line encounters a river
options: chaining is obstructed but ranging is free
ranging is obstructed but chaining is free
both ranging and chaining are obstructed
both ranging and chaining are free
explain: When a chain line crosses a river, physical chaining across the water is obstructed, but ranging (establishing the line of sight/direction) remains possible since both banks are typically visible.

q: 28. Reciprocal ranging is adopted when the following is encountered
explain: Reciprocal ranging is used when the end stations of a chain line are mutually invisible due to intervening obstacles like a river, where surveyors cannot see each other's ranging rods directly.

q: 29. Indirect ranging is adopted when the two ends of chain line are
explain: Indirect (random line) ranging is used specifically when the two end stations of the chain line cannot see each other directly, i.e., they are mutually invisible.

q: 30. A 30 m chain after measuring a distance of 6000 m was found to be 10 cm more than the designated length. If the chain was standardized before the commencement of survey than the true length is
explain: Since the chain elongated during use (became 30.1 m instead of 30 m by the end), the measured length is an underestimate; true length = measured length x (actual chain length/nominal length), giving approximately 6010 m.

q: 31. Handles are connected to the link by
explain: The handles of a chain are connected to the end links via a swivel joint, which allows the chain to be turned without twisting or kinking the links.

q: 32. A chain may get elongated due to
explain: A chain elongates mainly due to the opening out (wear and stretching) of the connecting rings between links over repeated use, per the book's answer key, though temperature and pull can also contribute.

q: 33. A chain is made up mild steel or galvanized iron wire of diameter
explain: A standard surveying chain is made of mild steel or galvanized iron wire of about 4 mm diameter.

q: 34. The walk step of a man is considered equal to:
explain: For the purpose of measuring distance by pacing, an average man's walking step (pace length) is conventionally taken as about 80 cm.

q: 35. Offsets are
explain: An offset is defined as a short lateral measurement taken from the chain line to locate a detail point lying off the chain line.

q: 36. The error in measured length due to bad ranging is
options: sometimes compensating error and sometimes cumulative error
explain: Bad ranging always makes the measured line longer than the true straight distance (a zig-zag path is longer than a straight one), so the error is always in the same (positive) direction, making it cumulative.

q: 37. An invar tape is generally used for accurate measurement of distance because it possesses ... coefficient of thermal expansion
explain: Invar (a nickel-steel alloy) has a very low coefficient of thermal expansion, making tapes made from it far less sensitive to temperature-induced length changes, ideal for precise base line measurement.

q: 38. When a chain is used at a temperature more than the temperature it was calibrated, the error in measured length will be
explain: A chain used at a higher temperature than its standardisation temperature expands, so it becomes effectively too long for every measurement, making the resulting error cumulative (in one consistent direction).

q: 39. The instrument attached to the wheel of a vehicle in order to measure the distance travelled, is called
explain: An odometer is fitted to a vehicle's wheel to measure the total distance travelled by counting wheel rotations.

q: 40. It is more convenient and gives better results while measuring horizontal distance ... by stepping method
explain: Stepping method for measuring horizontal distance on sloping ground gives better, more convenient results when done downhill, since gravity assists in maintaining a horizontal tape segment.

q: 41. Negative errors are causes in chain, when its length is
explain: If the actual chain is longer than its nominal/standard length, every measured distance comes out shorter than the true distance, resulting in a negative error.

q: 42. The maximum allowable limit up to that a measurement may vary from the true value is known as
explain: The permissible error is defined as the maximum allowable deviation of a measured value from its true value, within the specified precision of the survey.

q: 43. The permissible limits of error in chaining for measurement on rough of hilly ground is
explain: For chaining on rough or hilly ground, where conditions are difficult, a comparatively lower precision of about 1 in 250 is considered permissible.

q: 44. The position of point can be fixed more accurately by
explain: Fixing a point by oblique offsets (measuring two distances from different known points to the same detail point) generally gives a more accurate check/fix on its position than a single perpendicular offset.

q: 45. Invar tapes are made of an alloy of
explain: Invar is a special low-thermal-expansion alloy of nickel (about 36%) and steel, used for making tapes/wires requiring high dimensional stability with temperature.

q: 46. An obstacle which obstructs both chaining and ranging may be
explain: A building lying directly in the path of a survey line obstructs both the direct line of sight (ranging) and the physical laying of the chain (chaining) across it.

q: 47. The error due to bad ranging is
explain: As per the book's answer key, the error due to bad ranging (random deviations from the true line) is treated as a compensating error, tending to partially cancel out over a series of measurements.

q: 48. In order to locate a point by oblique offsets we must measure and note at least
explain: Locating a point by the method of oblique offsets requires measuring two distances (offsets) from two different points on the chain line to the detail point.

q: 49. Offsets are
options: ties or check lines which are perpendicular to chain line
sets of minor instruments in chain surveying
chain lines which go out of alignment
explain: Offsets are lateral (typically short) measurements or ties, often perpendicular, taken from the chain line to locate the position of nearby details/objects.

q: 50. A line which joins subsidiary stations on the main lines of a chain survey network and serves to facilitate taking offsets to objects located at great distances from the main survey lines as called
explain: By definition, a tie line joins two subsidiary points on the main chain lines and is used to take offsets to distant detail points, keeping the offsets short.
